archetypes.name: architecture
archetypes.rationale: Plan specifies a monolithic design-step0.sh with --phase flags, but the new test harness assert_wrapper_contract_pins references design-step0-parse.sh, design-step0-session.sh, design-step0-degraded.sh, design-step0-route.sh, and design-step0-init.sh as separate scripts; design-step6.sh is likewise split into design-step6-prelude.sh and design-step6-cleanup.sh. These naming divergences cascade through SKILL.md Bash fences, test assertions, and .md sibling contracts.
archetypes.prompt_body: Review whether the naming split (design-step0-parse/session/degraded/route/init instead of a monolithic design-step0.sh with --phase flags, and design-step6-prelude/cleanup instead of a unified design-step6.sh) is intentional and internally consistent across SKILL.md Bash fences, assert_wrapper_contract_pins, assert_design_skill_bash_fences_are_wrappers, and the plan spec. Check that every name referenced by the new test assertions actually has a committed executable script and a sibling .md file. Verify that the split does not introduce gaps such as a pause-check contract that is now split across two wrappers with no clear ordering guarantee. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: risk-integration
archetypes.rationale: The new assert_design_skill_bash_fences_are_wrappers Python check at approximately line 378 requires --claude-pid on every bash fence, not only Step 0 and Step 5c wrappers as stated in the plan; this would cause immediate CI failure unless all wrappers accept and forward the flag. The harness also drops from ~2050 to 339 lines, removing self-tests, inline fence behavioral checks, and postplan thin-fence self-tests without equivalent coverage in the new wrapper contract pins.
archetypes.prompt_body: Check whether assert_design_skill_bash_fences_are_wrappers in the new scripts/test-design-structure.sh requires --claude-pid on every Bash fence or only on Step 0 and Step 5c fences; the plan restricts this flag to those two wrappers and any over-requirement would break CI. Audit whether the dropped checks (assert_thin_fence, assert_postplan_thin_fence, run_thin_fence_self_tests, assert_design_route_pause_integration, Step 0-pre/0b block extraction checks, and folded-sentinel ordering checks) have documented equivalents in the new wrapper contract pins or are silently unguarded. Verify that the boundary_markers list in assert_no_consecutive_executable_script_call_fences covers the real SKILL.md section headers introduced by the wrapper refactor. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.
